content:
Petra Zlatarić-Novosel
Osijek, Croatia | petra.zlataric@example.com | +385 55 555 0606

Dear Quillstone Payments Hiring Team,

I am applying for the Machine Learning Engineer – Customer Support AI role. I am an ML engineer with more than five years of experience in applied machine learning and NLP, including taking document models from development into production. I hold an MSc in Computer Science and am currently pursuing a PhD focused on named entity recognition in Croatian legal texts.

At Slavonica Document AI, I developed and deployed an incoming-document classifier for public administration that achieves 94% accuracy and a 0.91 macro F1 across 23 classes, processing approximately 15,000 documents per day. I fine-tuned XLM-R and BERTić models and delivered them as FastAPI services in Docker on Azure App Service, using Azure ML and MLflow. I also established weekly production monitoring; it identified an OCR change that reduced accuracy by nine percentage points, allowing the issue to be resolved within a week.

My earlier work at Baranjska kreditna banka is directly relevant to customer support: I built an 11-topic classifier for customer complaints, progressing from a TF-IDF and logistic-regression baseline to fastText. Its outputs supported weekly reporting to customer service management. I have also built a weekend prototype for question answering over Croatian laws using sentence embeddings, FAISS and an open-weight LLM accessed through an API. Alongside my production experience, this has given me hands-on familiarity with retrieval-augmented question answering.

I am keen to bring my experience in NLP, model serving and monitoring to Quillstone’s AI team as it builds tools to answer merchant questions and support customer operations. The team’s emphasis on ownership, practical problem-solving and learning together particularly appeals to me. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my background could contribute to the role.

Kind regards,
Petra Zlatarić-Novosel

critique.content_quality_feedback: The cover letter is concise, professional, and well targeted. It presents strong quantified evidence from the document-classification role, connects customer-complaint classification to the customer-support context, and accurately describes the RAG experience as a prototype. The progression from production NLP systems to customer-support-related text classification is logical and convincing. The main content weakness is that several relevant capabilities present in the candidate material—strong Python, MLOps, and model registry/versioning—are not explicitly stated in the letter.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The letter uses a clean, conventional structure that should parse well in ATS and AI screening systems: clear contact details, salutation, short paragraphs, standard terminology, and no problematic tables or graphics. It includes important keywords such as NLP, production, model serving, monitoring, FastAPI, Docker, Azure, Azure ML, MLflow, RAG, sentence embeddings, and FAISS. AI screening probability is high but not optimal because the letter does not explicitly include the exact terms Python, MLOps, model registry or model versioning, and it does not address feature engineering or data ingestion pipelines. Those last capabilities are not established in the candidate material and should not be added as claims.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The document aligns strongly with the role's NLP, production ML, model-serving, monitoring, Azure, and RAG requirements. The customer-complaint classifier is a particularly relevant example for Customer Support AI, while the document-classification system demonstrates meaningful production scale and operational ownership. The letter also appropriately reflects Quillstone's emphasis on ownership, practical problem-solving, and learning together. Candidate-material gaps remain for the requirement of at least four years specifically as a machine learning engineer shipping systems to production, and for feature engineering and data ingestion pipelines. The candidate has more than five years of broader applied ML experience, but the supplied timeline does not clearly establish four years under the Machine Learning Engineer role or equivalent production ML engineering scope.
critique.improvement_instructions:
CRITICAL / HIGH-VALUE: In the second paragraph, after the sentence ending "using Azure ML and MLflow," add the supported production-engineering detail: "I used MLflow for experiment tracking and model registry, alongside strong Python-based development for production model serving." This makes the model versioning/model registry and Python keywords explicit without adding unsupported tools or experience.

HIGH-VALUE: In the third paragraph, revise the sentence beginning "Alongside my production experience" to make the RAG scope precise while preserving credibility: "Although this was a personal prototype rather than a production system, it gave me hands-on experience with retrieval-augmented question answering using sentence embeddings, FAISS and an open-weight LLM accessed through an API." This directly matches the RAG requirement and clearly distinguishes prototype experience from production experience.

MINOR ATS ENHANCEMENT: In the final paragraph, change "my experience in NLP, model serving and monitoring" to "my experience in NLP, Python-based model serving, production monitoring and MLOps with Azure ML and MLflow." Use this only as a summary of the experience already documented in the candidate material.

My earlier work at Baranjska kreditna banka is directly relevant to customer support: I built an 11-topic classifier for customer complaints, progressing from a TF-IDF and logistic-regression baseline to fastText. I am keen to bring my experience in NLP, Python-based model serving, production monitoring and MLOps with Azure ML and MLflow to Quillstone’s AI team as it builds tools to answer merchant questions and support customer operations. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my background could contribute to the role.

critique.content_quality_feedback: The cover letter is clear, professional, well structured, and appropriately tailored to the Machine Learning Engineer – Customer Support AI role. It presents quantified production impact, relevant NLP experience, cloud deployment, model serving, monitoring, and the customer-complaint classification project. The candid qualification of the RAG work as a personal, non-production prototype strengthens credibility. The main content opportunity is to make the candidate’s dataset-building and text-data preparation experience more visible, since these are relevant to the role and supported by the candidate information.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The letter is ATS-friendly: it uses standard headings and paragraphs, contains no complex tables or graphics, and includes relevant terms such as NLP, Python, FastAPI, Docker, Azure App Service, Azure ML, MLflow, model serving, production monitoring, sentence embeddings, FAISS, and retrieval-augmented question answering. AI screening probability is good because the letter contains strong role-specific keywords and measurable outcomes. It does not explicitly mention data ingestion pipelines, feature engineering, or data versioning; however, the supplied candidate material does not substantiate these areas, so they should not be added as claims. The RAG terminology is present and accurately qualified.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: Alignment is strong for production NLP, document AI, model serving, cloud deployment, monitoring, MLOps, Python, and customer-support text classification. The letter also connects the candidate’s complaint-classification work to customer support and appropriately relates the RAG prototype to the company’s AI-assistant focus. The candidate has the required computer science degree and Azure experience. The candidate’s material does not clearly establish four full years specifically as an ML engineer shipping systems to production: the ML Engineer role begins in 2023, while earlier work is described as Data Scientist and Research Project Assistant. The candidate’s material also does not substantiate data versioning, feature engineering, or data-ingestion pipelines. These are requirement gaps rather than defects that can be corrected through wording. The culture paragraph is appropriately aligned with the advertisement’s ownership, practical problem-solving, and learning themes without making unsupported claims.
critique.improvement_instructions:
MINOR, HIGH-VALUE IMPROVEMENT — In the third paragraph, immediately after the sentence ending “within a week,” add a sentence supported by the candidate information: “I also built and annotated a dataset of 4,000 Croatian administrative documents, creating annotation guidelines and achieving an inter-annotator Cohen’s kappa of 0.87 with two annotators.” This makes the candidate’s experience preparing and annotating large text datasets more visible and strengthens alignment with the role’s dataset and data-preparation responsibilities.

MINOR PRECISION IMPROVEMENT — In the second paragraph, change “I am an ML engineer with more than five years of experience in applied machine learning and NLP” to “I am a machine learning professional with more than five years of experience in applied machine learning and NLP, including production model deployment.” This avoids implying more than five years specifically under the ML Engineer job title while preserving the supported experience claim.
